headline_marked: Cristiano Ronaldo [[accuses coach of broken promises]] after leaving Portugal camp
headline: Cristiano Ronaldo accuses coach of broken promises after leaving Portugal camp
summary: The football superstar claims coach Jorge Jesus broke his word twice, leading to his departure from the national team. Ronaldo insists he remains available for future matches.
details: Cristiano Ronaldo has publicly accused Portugal's coach Jorge Jesus of making and breaking promises, which led to his abrupt departure from the national team's camp. The star forward stated that an agreement to manage his fitness by missing two matches was reneged upon when he was told to warm up for a game he was not going to play in.

Ronaldo detailed a subsequent meeting where an eight-point document was prepared, outlining that he never demanded playing time and respected the coach's decisions. He claims the coach's public statements about the incident did not align with their private discussion, marking the second time Jesus had allegedly broken his word.

The football icon expressed his decision to leave the training camp without waiting for further broken promises. He apologized for not greeting supporters and leaving his teammates, acknowledging the seriousness of his actions as captain.

Despite the current rupture, Ronaldo stated his international ambitions remain strong. He affirmed his availability to compete for Portugal after serving any imposed suspension, provided he is physically fit and performing well for his club.

Coach Jorge Jesus has denied making any agreement with Ronaldo but has left the door open for the player's potential return to the national squad. The Portuguese Football Federation has yet to issue an official comment on Ronaldo's statement.

headline_marked: [[Child kidnappers]] abandon 6-year-old after failed sale attempt
headline: Child kidnappers abandon 6-year-old after failed sale attempt
summary: A child trafficking ring abducted a six-year-old boy from his home in Dhaka. After failing to sell him in Gazipur, they abandoned him on the street, leading to his rescue 18 days later.
details: A six-year-old boy, abducted from his home in Rupnagar, Dhaka, has been rescued after 18 days. The child was taken by a gang intending to sell him, but their plan was thwarted by police and the Special Response Battalion (SRB). The kidnappers eventually abandoned the child on the street in Gazipur when they couldn't complete the sale.

The boy disappeared from his home on September 18 while his father was present. After discovering his son missing, the father filed a case with the Rupnagar police station. The SRB initiated a shadow investigation to locate the child.

Analysis of CCTV footage revealed the child being led away from his home by two women, identified as Nasrin and Kulsum, approximately 1.5 kilometers away. No further footage was available after this point.

Investigators learned that Nasrin, a tenant's daughter from a neighboring house, was a member of a child trafficking ring. She, along with Kulsum, abducted the child for sale. Police have arrested Kulsum in connection with the incident.

The SRB reported that the child was taken to Gazipur and attempts were made to sell him there. However, sensing increased law enforcement activity, the kidnappers abandoned him. A patrolling police unit found the child and took him to a child rehabilitation center in Tongi East Police Station area as he could not provide his name or address.
The SRB rescued the child from the rehabilitation center on Tuesday. Efforts are ongoing to arrest the remaining members of the trafficking ring.
